'''''Bunium bulbocastanum''''' is a plant [[species]] in the family [[Apiaceae]]. 
It was once used as a root vegetable in parts of western Europe, and has been called '''great pignut'''<ref name=GRINb>{{GRIN | ''Bunium bulbocastanum'' | 316877 | accessdate = 1 January 2018}}</ref><ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> or '''earthnut'''.<ref name=GRINb/> 

==Growth==
The plant is native to western Europe.<ref name="POWO_838875-1">{{citation |title=''Bunium bulbocastanum'' <small>L.</small> |work=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew|url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:838875-1 |accessdate=2018-06-30}}</ref> It reaches about {{convert|60|cm|in|abbr=on}} tall and {{convert|25|cm|in|abbr=on}} wide, bearing frilly leaves and hermaphroditic flowers; it is pollinated by insects and self-fertile.{{citation needed|date=October 2013}}

The small, rounded [[taproot]] is edible raw or cooked, and said to taste like sweet [[chestnut]]s.{{citation needed|date=October 2013}} The leaf can be used as an [[herb]] or [[garnish (food)|garnish]] similar to [[parsley]].
